distractors.reason: 'Wide' describes physical extent (a wide road, a wide river). We don't say 'wide generalization' because a claim is not measured in width.
'Big' only signals size. A sweeping generalization is about scope and dismissiveness, not quantity, so 'big generalization' loses the nuance.
'Huge' is an intensifier of size or amount. It does not carry the idea of a broad claim that ignores exceptions, so it is not used with 'generalization'.

example_sentence: That is a ___ generalization that ignores all the evidence.
l1_interference: Türkçe konuşanlar genellikle 'büyük' sıfatını her yere getirir ve 'big generalization' der, oysa doğrusu 'sweeping generalization'dır. 'Geniş' anlamındaki 'wide' de burada yanlış olur.
explanation: 'Sweeping' suggests a claim that covers too much ground and overlooks exceptions. The adjective carries a critical connotation, which is why it is the natural choice in argumentative writing.

related_collocations.example: The new law brought sweeping changes to the education system.
The committee was given sweeping powers to investigate the case.
His sweeping statement offended many of the people in the room.

memory_tip: SWEEPING = covers everything, ignores exceptions (sweeping generalization, sweeping changes) | BIG/HUGE = size only, not scope
